newsitem.title: USA: U.S. tells Afghan embassy to close.
newsitem.headline: U.S. tells Afghan embassy to close.

text.p: The United States told the Afghan embassy in Washington on Thursday to close down because it does not want to appear partial towards the fundamentalist Taleban movement, which controls the Afghan capital.
"The Department of State has decided to suspend temporarily operations at the Afghanistan embassy in Washington, effective August 21st," department spokesman James Rubin said.
"We concluded that the result of not taking this action would be that one representative of the Taleban would end up being in charge -- that would send a signal that we were not neutral," he added.

The Afghan embassy has two diplomats in dispute over who represents the country. They are Seraj Jamal, nominated charge d'affaires by the Taleban, and former charge d'affaires Yar Mohammad Mohabbat, an appointee of the old government.
In May the Taleban asked Mohabbat to give up his post in favor of Jamal but the State Department has not accredited Jamal as his successor, added the source.

Rubin said the Afghan diplomats could stay in the United States as representatives of Afghan political factions. "If they want to stay and serve as a faction representer, they would have to do it from some other place (outside the embassy building)," he added.
